_about: Hand-gathered commentary: characteristic gamaka and prayogas, mood, time of
day, associated deities. Fields 10-13 of specs/06-raga-detail-page.md.
This file is deliberately separate from data/ragas.json, and deliberately
empty. ragas.json is what a scraper read from a source; this is what a
person concluded from reading, listening or being taught. Mixing the two
would make one file with two kinds of confidence in it and no way to tell
which sentence carries which.
NO SOURCE PUBLISHES THIS. Checked 2026-08-02: gamaka and prayoga
descriptions live in teaching and in books; mood/rasa is real but contested
and school-dependent; deities attach to compositions more than to ragas;
and time of day is substantially a Hindustani framing, so for most Carnatic
ragas empty is the correct value rather than a gap. CLAUDE.md forbids
writing any of it from memory, and these are precisely the fields where an
invention would be indistinguishable from scholarship.
THE THREE RULES
1. No note without a citation. Every entry carries a `cite` that resolves
to the `citations` block below. validate_ragas.py check 10 fails on one
that does not, so this file cannot quietly accumulate remembered content
the way a free-text field would.
2. Citations are typed - `web`, `book`, `person` - because this will come
from websites and books and teachers, and a bare URL field would force a
book into the wrong shape. `person` means a human with the training to
judge it, the same standing it carries in data/source_reviews.json.
3. More than one entry per field is expected. Two sources disagreeing about
a raga's mood is information; the page shows both, each with its own
credit, rather than picking one and hiding the other.
NO SWARA NAMES IN PROSE - the same rule data/source_reviews.json carries,
and it matters more here, because a note about gamaka is prose about swaras
almost by definition. A label depends on the reader's numbering convention
(CLAUDE.md, 'Notation format'), so a scale spelled into a sentence is right
for one reader and wrong for another. Put the degrees in a `scales` object
on the entry and reference them from the text as {name}; the page renders
each one under whatever convention the reader has chosen.
SHAPE (an entry, once there is one to write):
"citations": {
"<id>": {"type": "book", "author": "…", "title": "…",
"page": "…", "url": null, "accessed": null}
"ragas": {
"<raga id>": {
"gamaka":      [{"text": "… {phrase} …", "cite": "<id>",
"scales": {"phrase": [{"degree": 0, "label": "S"}]}}],
"prayogas":    [],
"mood":        [],
"time_of_day": [],
"deities":     []
Run scripts/coverage_report.py to see how empty this is and stay honest
about it.
